prompt:
You are a credit rating analyst. Using only the information below and general knowledge predating 2026-04-23, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify).
Valid answers (choose exactly one): AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Company information (as of 2026-04-23):
| Current ratio           | 0.35 |
| Retained earnings       | 26,088M |
| Current liabilities     | 159,640M |
| Current assets          | 56,524M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 33,995M |
| Total liabilities       | 274,899M |
| Total assets            | 308,894M |
| EBIT / operating income | 6,598M |
| Revenue                 | 20,880M |
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The company shows extremely weak liquidity (current ratio ~0.35) and very high leverage (total liabilities far exceeding equity), with limited cushion to cover obligations. While EBIT is positive, the combination of poor liquidity and high debt suggests significant default risk absent earnings durability or asset protection. On the 21-grade scale, this profile fits a highly speculative, near-non-investment-grade rating.

DECISION: BB-
